notes: Verbatim check: every sourceSays was matched against the live page text on 2026-10-07. Most pages were fetched with curl. Miami, Doral, Pinecrest, Sunny Isles Beach, Hialeah Gardens and Miami Springs block bots (403), so we read those in a headless browser.

Expect changes after the 3 Nov 2026 election. Mayor certain to change: Cutler Bay, Palmetto Bay and Opa-locka (open seats); Pinecrest (Shannon del Prado, unopposed); Key Biscayne (Brett Moss, unopposed); Biscayne Park (Groth's commission seat expires and he is not running). Incumbent faces a challenger: Coral Gables, North Miami, Aventura, Sunny Isles Beach, El Portal and Virginia Gardens. Re-check after 3 Nov. Runoffs, where needed, fall on 17 Nov (El Portal, Pinecrest), 1 Dec (Coral Gables, Cutler Bay, Palmetto Bay, Sunny Isles Beach) and 8 Dec (Opa-locka; only two candidates, so unlikely).

Council-chosen mayors who can change without a citywide vote: Bal Harbour (picked at the November induction meeting, so possibly Nov 2026); Biscayne Park (after the Nov 2026 election); Bay Harbor Islands (after the April 2027 election); Indian Creek Village (after each February election, the last in Feb 2026); Miami Shores (two-year mayoralty, next Village election April 2027).

Most ballot details in termNote come from one secondary source: Florida Politics, 'Municipal elections abound in Miami-Dade this November' (Jesse Scheckner, 15 Sep 2026, republished by The Miami Times). Other news sources: Key Biscayne Independent, Local10, WLRN and Diario las Americas.

Recent changes a stale list would miss: Hialeah (Bryan Calvo, Nov 2025, replacing interim mayor Jacqueline Garcia-Roves); Miami (Eileen Higgins, Dec 2025); Florida City (Charlotte Thompson, early 2026, replacing Otis Wallace); Surfside (Shlomo Danzinger, Apr 2026, replacing Charles Burkett); Bal Harbour (Seth Salver, Nov 2025, replacing Jeffrey Freimark); Medley (Lily Stefano, Nov 2024); Miami Lakes (Joshua Dieguez, Nov 2024); North Miami Beach (Michael Joseph, Dec 2024).

Do NOT use miamidade.gov/commission/library/local-mayors-list.pdf. It is years out of date: it lists Regalado for Miami, Levine for Miami Beach and Gilbert for Miami Gardens. The Miami-Dade League of Cities officials list (miamidade.gov/resources/intergovernmental-affairs/documents/municipality-directory.pdf, 'Updated 10/1/2025') predates the Nov 2025 to Apr 2026 elections. Use it only as a cross-check. The old miamishoresvillage.com domain may also be stale; the current site is msvfl.gov.

Medium confidence, Hialeah Gardens: the official page still lists De La Cruz, but its bio text is clearly old ('currently the youngest Mayor in Miami-Dade County'). We could not find the result of the 4 Mar 2025 mayoral election. Confirm with the City Clerk or the county elections results.

Medium confidence, West Miami: the official bio mentions only the 2024 re-election. Local10 and Diario las Americas report that Diaz-Padron was re-elected on 14 Apr 2026 and sworn in 20 Apr 2026, so the name is current.

Selection method for Biscayne Park (council) rests on a 2013 Shutts & Bowen release about Coviello being 'selected... by his colleagues'. We did not read the charter text. Bal Harbour (council) is confirmed by its induction agenda item 'ELECTION OF MAYOR & VICE MAYOR'. Golden Beach (elected) is inferred from the official bio ('successfully ran for Mayor') and a 2007 county mayoral ballot.

All titles are plain 'Mayor'. None of the official pages we checked uses 'Village Mayor' or 'Executive Mayor'. Kendall, Westchester and other unincorporated areas are excluded; their residents' mayor is the county mayor.
